# readboj

`readboj` is an R client for the official [Bank of Japan (BoJ)
Time-Series Data Search](https://www.stat-search.boj.or.jp/) API and
selected official download surfaces. It is for analysts, researchers,
and reproducible data pipelines that need to discover series, read
observations, retain the exact source response, and replay a result
offline.

The package works directly with allow-listed official BoJ HTTPS hosts.
Each successful response or file is identified by a SHA-256 hash in the
returned provenance, and bounded caches support connected and offline
workflows. Version 0.2.0 is distributed from the private GitHub
repository.

## Install

Install the current GitHub version with:

``` r

install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("chartwell-macro/readboj")
```

Installation requires access to the GitHub repository. If the repository
is private or your network restricts GitHub, configure a GitHub personal
access token or another authentication method supported by `pak`. This
is separate from the supported public BoJ routes, which do not require
BoJ credentials (see [Network, credentials, and cache
behaviour](#network-credentials-and-cache-behaviour)).

CRAN installation becomes available after the package is accepted there:

``` r

install.packages("readboj")
```

For the current development release, use the GitHub installation above.

## Retrieve and chart a time series

This end-to-end workflow searches the official metadata catalogue,
selects the exact monthly exchange-rate series `FM08/FXERM07`, retrieves
its 2025 observations, keeps valid `date`/`value` rows, and draws a line
chart. Set `READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES=true` to run the bounded official API
calls while rendering. The default documentation build displays a
checked-in rendering of the same verified response, keeping CRAN and
pkgdown builds deterministic and offline.

``` r

cache <- file.path(tempdir(), "readboj-chart-cache")
matches <- search_boj_series(
  query = "FXERM07", db = "FM08", language = "en", limit = 10L,
  cache_dir = cache, deadline = Sys.time() + 90
)
selected <- matches[matches$series_code == "FXERM07", , drop = FALSE]
stopifnot(nrow(selected) == 1L)

series <- read_boj_series(
  db = selected$db[[1]], code = selected$series_code[[1]],
  start_date = "202501", end_date = "202512", language = "en",
  cache_dir = cache, deadline = Sys.time() + 90
)
chart_data <- series[
  !is.na(series$date) & is.finite(series$value),
  c("date", "value")
]
stopifnot(nrow(chart_data) > 1L)
```

``` r

if (requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    chart_data,
    ggplot2::aes(x = date, y = value)
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_line() +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = "Yen per U.S. dollar in 2025",
      subtitle = "Monthly published observations",
      x = "Month",
      y = "Yen per U.S. dollar",
      caption = "Source: Bank of Japan Time-Series Data Search API"
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
}
```

![Line chart of the monthly yen per U.S. dollar spot rate during 2025,
falling through April and rising through
December.](reference/figures/readboj-fxerm07-2025.png)

The rendered example uses the official series *US.Dollar/Yen Spot Rate
at 17:00 in JST, Average in the Month, Tokyo Market* (`FM08/FXERM07`;
yen per U.S. dollar), periods `202501`–`202512`. Its response and figure
hashes, retrieval time, source URL, and upstream terms are recorded in
`inst/NOTICE/boj-chart-source.txt`. It is a readboj documentation chart,
not an official BoJ chart or a bundled raw-data snapshot.

## Parse a response offline

The package ships tiny **synthetic structural fixtures** (separate from
the saved Outlook history) for parser and documentation examples. They
are not official BoJ observations. This example uses one fixture to
exercise the real local parser, including dates, a missing observation,
and provenance:

``` r

library(readboj)

fixture <- system.file("extdata", "api-data-page-1.json", package = "readboj")
if (!nzchar(fixture)) fixture <- file.path("inst", "extdata", "api-data-page-1.json")

observations <- read_boj_snapshot(
  fixture,
  type = "data_json",
  db = "FM08"
)

observations[, c("series_code", "period", "date", "value", "value_status")]
#>   series_code period       date  value value_status
#> 1    SYNTHM01 202601 2026-01-01 101.25     observed
#> 2    SYNTHM01 202602 2026-02-01     NA         null
#> 3    SYNTHM01 202603 2026-03-01 103.75     observed
```

The fixture deliberately contains the series code `SYNTHM01`, the values
`101.25`, `NA`, and `103.75`, and the message `Synthetic success`. Treat
it as an executable parser example, not as a data source or a claim
about an FM08 series.

For an online request, replace the fixture with an exact BoJ database
and series code.
[`read_boj_series()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_series.md)
follows the API’s pagination cursor and preserves missing rows:

``` r

if (identical(Sys.getenv("READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES"), "true")) {
  fx <- read_boj_series(
    db = "FM08",
    code = "FXERM07",
    start_date = "202601",
    end_date = "202606",
    cache_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "readboj-live-example-cache"),
    timeout = 10,
    retries = 0L,
    wait = 0,
    max_bytes = 8 * 1024^2,
    max_pages = 2L,
    max_cells = 1000L,
    max_codes_total = 1L,
    deadline = Sys.time() + 30
  )
  boj_provenance(fx)
} else {
  message("Set READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES=true to run this live example.")
}
```

The online example is intentionally shown as code rather than run while
this README is built: API availability and current revisions are
external state.

## What the package covers

| User job | Main functions | Official surface | Offline/local path |
|----|----|----|----|
| Find a database or series | [`boj_databases()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_databases.md), [`search_boj_series()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/search_boj_series.md), [`boj_metadata()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_metadata.md) | Versioned API database registry and `getMetadata` | Search a cached response or a pinned catalogue |
| Read exact observations | [`read_boj_series()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_series.md), [`read_boj_layer()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_layer.md) | `getDataCode` and `getDataLayer` | [`read_boj_snapshot()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_snapshot.md) on a retained response |
| Pin a searchable catalogue | [`build_boj_catalogue_snapshot()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/build_boj_catalogue_snapshot.md), [`search_boj_catalogue_snapshot()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/search_boj_catalogue_snapshot.md) | Selected `getMetadata` CSV responses | Fully offline, hash-checked directory |
| Work with official bulk files | [`list_boj_bulk_files()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/list_boj_bulk_files.md), [`download_boj_bulk()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/download_boj_bulk.md), [`read_boj_bulk()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_bulk.md) | Current official bulk/download catalogue | Parse a local ZIP or CSV; cached downloads can be replayed |
| Work with dated Tankan releases | [`list_boj_tankan_releases()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/list_boj_tankan_releases.md), [`list_boj_tankan_assets()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/list_boj_tankan_assets.md), [`download_boj_tankan_asset()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/download_boj_tankan_asset.md), [`read_boj_workbook()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_workbook.md) | Dated comprehensive-data release pages and XLS/XLSX/ZIP assets | Parse a local downloaded asset |
| Inspect identity and service terms | [`boj_provenance()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_provenance.md), [`boj_api_credit()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_api_credit.md), [`boj_cache_prune()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_cache_prune.md) | Exact response/file identity and BoJ service notices | Provenance remains available after local replay |

The registry currently describes 50 database identifiers from the
February 18, 2026 API manual.
[`boj_databases()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_databases.md)
returns their bilingual names, categories, and manual revision. The
registry is a transcription of the official manual; its provenance also
records that source. The package’s bundled notice records `bojapi` as
lineage for parts of the registry/API parsing design; this is separate
from the official BoJ source and from the readboj MIT licence.

## Common workflows

### Discover and retrieve other series

The [chart workflow](#retrieve-and-chart-a-time-series) demonstrates
bounded metadata search followed by exact-series retrieval. Search is
bilingual and matches series codes, names, categories, and notes. For
large databases such as Tankan,
[`search_boj_series()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/search_boj_series.md)
scans the CSV in chunks instead of eagerly materialising it. Use
[`read_boj_layer()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_layer.md)
when the official hierarchy and frequency are the starting point, or
`format = "csv"` when retaining the official CSV representation is
important; Japanese CSV responses are decoded as CP932.

### Make a portable catalogue snapshot

For a repeatable discovery workflow, build a directory containing
immutable metadata objects and manifests, then search it without
contacting BoJ:

``` r

if (identical(Sys.getenv("READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES"), "true")) {
  catalogue_dir <- tempfile("readboj-catalogue-")
  manifest <- build_boj_catalogue_snapshot(
    catalogue_dir, db = "FM08", language = "both",
    cache_dir = file.path(tempdir(), "readboj-live-example-cache"),
    timeout = 10, retries = 0L, wait = 0, max_bytes = 8 * 1024^2,
    max_databases = 1L, max_rows_per_db = 10000L,
    max_total_bytes = 64 * 1024^2, deadline = Sys.time() + 60
  )
  search_boj_catalogue_snapshot(catalogue_dir, "dollar", db = "FM08")
} else {
  message("Set READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES=true to run this live example.")
}
```

Pass `db = boj_databases()$db` to select the full declared 50-database
surface, subject to the configured size and time bounds. The generated
`manifest.csv` records row counts, date ranges, raw hashes, and whether
each selected database was complete within its own request.

### Read bulk files and workbooks

The bulk and Tankan functions separate discovery, download, and parsing.
A download returns a `boj_file` path with immutable source provenance;
parsers accept that path or an ordinary local file:

``` r

if (identical(Sys.getenv("READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES"), "true")) {
  cache <- file.path(tempdir(), "readboj-live-example-cache")
  # Inspect the returned tables before selecting and downloading a file.
  bulk_catalogue <- list_boj_bulk_files(
    language = "en", cache_dir = cache,
    timeout = 10, retries = 0L, wait = 0, max_bytes = 2 * 1024^2,
    deadline = Sys.time() + 30
  )
  releases <- list_boj_tankan_releases(
    language = "en", cache_dir = cache, max_pages = 6L,
    timeout = 10, retries = 0L, wait = 0, max_bytes = 2 * 1024^2,
    deadline = Sys.time() + 60
  )
  if (nrow(releases)) {
    assets <- list_boj_tankan_assets(
      releases$url[[1]], cache_dir = cache,
      timeout = 10, retries = 0L, wait = 0, max_bytes = 2 * 1024^2,
      deadline = Sys.time() + 30
    )
  }
} else {
  message("Set READBOJ_LIVE_EXAMPLES=true to run this live example.")
}
```

[`read_boj_bulk()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_bulk.md)
returns a data frame for a single CSV, or a named list of data frames
for a ZIP with multiple CSV members.
[`read_boj_workbook()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_workbook.md)
returns a named list of text-valued data frames; text preservation keeps
identifiers, labels, units, and suppression markers from being silently
coerced.

## Output and provenance contract

The public functions return base R structures with explicit, stable
contracts:

- Observation readers return a `data.frame` with columns `db`,
  `series_code`, bilingual names/units/categories, `frequency`,
  `last_update`, the exact string `period`, parsed `date`, numeric
  `value`, original `raw_value`, and `value_status`. API JSON `null`
  values and API CSV blanks remain rows, with `value` set to `NA` and
  the source representation retained in `raw_value` and `value_status`.
  In bulk files, `NA` and `ND` markers remain literal text rather than
  being treated as observed values. Dates are parsed from official
  period codes; the original period is retained.
- Metadata results use a `data.frame` with `db`, `series_code`, names,
  units, categories, five hierarchy layers, start/end times,
  `last_update`, notes, and `is_series`. Network metadata readers and
  catalogue searches remove the other language fields for
  `language = "en"` or `"jp"`; `language = "both"` retains both. A local
  `read_boj_snapshot(type = "metadata_csv")` always retains the
  bilingual schema and treats `language` as validation only.
- [`search_boj_series()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/search_boj_series.md)
  and
  [`search_boj_catalogue_snapshot()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/search_boj_catalogue_snapshot.md)
  retain at most `limit` matching rows. Group headings are excluded by
  default and can be requested with `include_groups = TRUE`.
- [`read_boj_bulk()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_bulk.md)
  returns text columns plus `value_numeric` and `value_status` when a
  recognised long-file schema is present. ZIP results carry member
  names; unsafe archive paths and size/row bounds fail closed.
- [`read_boj_workbook()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_workbook.md)
  returns a named list of text-valued data frames.
  [`download_boj_bulk()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/download_boj_bulk.md)
  and
  [`download_boj_tankan_asset()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/download_boj_tankan_asset.md)
  return a character path with class `c("boj_file", "character")`.
- Objects produced from a source response or file carry a
  `readboj_provenance` attribute. `boj_provenance(x)` extracts a
  producer-specific list. Network snapshots include canonical/final
  URLs, retrieval time, raw SHA-256, bytes, and cache identity; local
  parsers record a path, raw hash, bytes, and parser schema. Observation
  JSON/CSV provenance also reports a semantic hash that excludes only
  the volatile response `DATE` field.

Expected failures detected by package validation, transport, parsing,
cache, and identity checks use typed errors such as
`readboj_parameter_error`, `readboj_transport_error`,
`readboj_timeout_error`, `readboj_size_error`, `readboj_schema_error`,
`readboj_identity_error`, `readboj_cache_corruption_error`, and
`readboj_offline_error` make failure handling possible without matching
prose messages. Unexpected base or dependency errors can still surface
from manually corrupted local metadata or malformed third-party files;
preserve the input identity and report those cases. No duplicate
observation identity is silently collapsed.

## Network, credentials, and cache behaviour

No BoJ credentials are required for the public routes supported by this
package. Network access is opt-in through the functions that discover or
retrieve official sources. Requests use HTTPS and are restricted to
`www.stat-search.boj.or.jp` and `www.boj.or.jp`, including HTTPS-only
redirects. Timeouts, retries, retry waits, page counts, cell/row counts,
archive sizes, and download bytes are bounded arguments.

By default, successful response bodies are retained in
`tools::R_user_dir("readboj", "cache")`. Set `cache_dir` explicitly for
a project-managed location, or set `options(readboj.cache_dir = ...)`.
The content-addressed cache defaults to a maximum of 2 GiB and 1,000 raw
objects; `options(readboj.cache_max_bytes = ...)` and
`options(readboj.cache_max_entries = ...)` can tighten those bounds. Use
[`boj_cache_prune()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_cache_prune.md)
to apply explicit limits. Failed responses are not cached.

Set `offline = TRUE` to require a valid, sufficiently recent cached
snapshot and make no network request. For a completely portable
hand-off, use
[`build_boj_catalogue_snapshot()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/build_boj_catalogue_snapshot.md)
and
[`search_boj_catalogue_snapshot()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/search_boj_catalogue_snapshot.md),
or ship a response/file and parse it with
[`read_boj_snapshot()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_snapshot.md),
[`read_boj_bulk()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_bulk.md),
or
[`read_boj_workbook()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_workbook.md).

## Outlook Report forecasts

``` r

# Ordinary reads use saved numeric data: no HTTP, PDFs or Poppler.
releases <- list_boj_outlook_releases()
history <- read_boj_outlook("all", comparison = "all")
latest_gdp <- read_boj_outlook(measure = "real_gdp", statistic = "median")
boj_outlook_status()

# Calendar-aware maintenance runs separately from UI selections.
maintenance <- maintain_boj_outlook()
maintenance$next_due_at
# Explicit immediate data check remains available:
# update_boj_outlook()

# Explicit raw discovery/parsing remains general, including unseen editions.
raw <- read_boj_outlook_raw("latest", deadline = Sys.time() + 300)
```

The **67,628-byte** numeric bundle covers **74 editions, October 2000 to
July 2026**, with 4,142 rows and five explicit NA cells. Its rows
exactly match the verified complete-archive parser output. Saved reads
reuse the loaded table; `latest` selects the newest saved edition.
`refresh = TRUE` reloads saved data without contacting the source. Check
freshness with
[`boj_outlook_status()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_outlook_status.md).

The separate updater checks the archive and every primary/full-text
asset, including historical URLs. Conditional HTTP and source hashes
detect additions, changed links and revisions. Revisions that remove
existing logical scalars or fiscal targets fail by default; an
intentional removal requires the reviewed `allow_coverage_loss = TRUE`
opt-in and remains recorded in revision history. It reparses affected
editions, validates the whole candidate and publishes atomically into
the user’s directory. Ordinary reads consume that directory
automatically. Failed/partial updates preserve the last good data and
record an explicit failure; corrupt refreshes trigger a warning and
fallback. The package baseline is read-only.

Use `READBOJ_OUTLOOK_DATA_DIR` or
`options(readboj.outlook_data_dir = ...)` to configure one location for
the application and updater. The installed
`system.file("scripts", "outlook-daily.R", package = "readboj")` runs
once from a daily scheduler, or with `--watch` as a long-lived
application worker. The repository’s daily GitHub workflow runs the same
update contract in its own cache; it does not deliver data to installed
applications. No machine-global job is installed. Attempts are throttled
to one UTC day; `force = TRUE` bypasses that limit. A daily run
throttled after a failed attempt exits nonzero; watch mode reports the
failure once and reports recovery when it occurs. Raw update staging is
deleted; only bounded structured generations and status receipts remain.

Fiscal years run **1 April through 31 March**. Current/prior vintages,
printed medians, majority/all-member endpoints, WPI/CGPI and distinct
CPI definitions, actuals, conditional estimates and NA cells remain
separate. Ranges describe member dispersion, **not confidence
intervals**. Source hashes, raw cell text, HTML XPath/PDF cell
coordinates and table notes survive in the saved data.

New data does not require a package release.
[`maintain_boj_outlook()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/maintain_boj_outlook.md)
discovers the official Outlook dates and bank holidays, runs due daily
historical revision checks, probes cheaply around publication windows,
and updates its own next-due schedule. Bank’s View has no fixed release
time; full text is tracked separately at the official next-business-day
14:00 Tokyo rule. The maintenance call returns UTC ISO8601 times,
pending full text, calendar freshness and structured errors. An hourly
scheduler can call the installed script with `--maintenance --once`;
not-due calls only read small local state and perform no network or
numeric-data work. The parent/application provisions the actual
scheduler. Unknown future source structures can still require a
parser/package change.

Only explicit raw parsing, rebuilding or an update requiring PDF parsing
needs optional Poppler `pdftotext`. Ordinary saved reads work without
it. There is no dated admission list, and pre-2016 interim statements
are not invented as report editions. See [the data/update contract and
verification](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/docs/outlook.md),
[`?read_boj_outlook`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_outlook.md),
[`?update_boj_outlook`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/update_boj_outlook.md)
and
[`?build_boj_outlook_bundle`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/build_boj_outlook_bundle.md).

## Scope and limitations

`readboj` reads the official surfaces it can identify and verify; it is
not a general web scraper. API and normal bulk data expose current
history; dated Outlook and Tankan routes retain their documented release
identities.

- API and ordinary bulk requests expose current/latest revised history.
  Local snapshots prove exactly what this client retrieved and when, but
  are not labelled official first releases. Dated Tankan assets provide
  a separate release-specific path.
- The API manual registry is versioned. If BoJ changes database codes,
  fields, HTML structure, encodings, or file layouts, a package update
  may be needed.
- `CO` metadata is large and is refused by
  [`boj_metadata()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_metadata.md)
  unless `allow_large = TRUE` is explicit; use bounded
  [`search_boj_series()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/search_boj_series.md)
  for discovery.
- Layer requests remain subject to official hierarchy limits. Bulk ZIPs
  and workbooks are structurally parsed with safety bounds; the package
  does not infer arbitrary table semantics or silently splice series
  across breaks.
- Outlook Report forecasts use the separate report route described
  above. Monetary Policy Meeting decisions and other policy statements
  remain outside this statistical parser’s scope.
- Live availability, rate limits, revisions, and current official HTML
  are external conditions. Keep raw hashes and provenance with
  downstream data so a changed source is visible.

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | What to check |
|----|----|
| `readboj_offline_error` | The request is not cached, is older than `max_age`, or the cache directory is different from the one used to create it. |
| Timeout, connection, or rate-limit error | Retry later, keep the default bounded retries, lower the requested surface, or use a retained snapshot. Do not raise limits without a reason. |
| `readboj_schema_error` | The official response or HTML layout changed. Save the error’s provenance and report the exact function, source URL, package version, and platform. |
| `readboj_size_error` | The selected database/file exceeds a safety bound. Prefer chunked search, a smaller query, explicit `max_*` limits, or the appropriate bulk/release surface. |
| Japanese text is incorrect | Use `language = "jp"`/`"both"` for API metadata and preserve the official CP932 encoding when parsing a local response. |
| [`read_boj_workbook()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_workbook.md) cannot open a file | Confirm that the path is a regular XLS/XLSX file and that the workbook is not a ZIP-only asset; pass an exact sheet name if needed. |

When reporting a reproducible problem, include
[`sessionInfo()`](https://rdrr.io/r/utils/sessionInfo.html),
`packageVersion("readboj")`, the function call with credentials and
private paths removed, and
[`boj_provenance()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_provenance.md)
output where available. Hashes and typed errors are more useful than a
screenshot of a transient webpage.

## BoJ credit, licensing, and citation

For the prescribed service credit and current links, run:

``` r

boj_api_credit()
```

The Bank of Japan’s API notice and site copyright terms govern use of
the upstream service and materials. They are not replaced by the
`readboj` MIT licence. `inst/NOTICE/bojapi-MIT.txt` preserves the
separate MIT attribution for the registry/API parsing design lineage
informed by `bojapi`; it does not make `bojapi` a data source, imply
copied source, or change the readboj authorship.
`inst/NOTICE/boj-chart-source.txt` records the official API source and
terms for the derived documentation chart. The small files under
`inst/extdata/` include synthetic deterministic fixtures and the
separately identified saved Outlook history described above.

`readboj` is authored and maintained by Chartwell Macro. **Package code:
MIT, copyright Chartwell Macro.** That package licence does not reassign
rights in Bank of Japan data, publications, services, or other upstream
material. To cite the package in a manuscript or report, use
`citation("readboj")` after installing it, or cite the repository at
<https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readboj>. Cite the Bank of Japan
separately when your work uses data retrieved from its service.

Outlook publications and graphics retain the Bank of Japan’s separate
rights. Retain `Source: Bank of Japan` and the exact source links.
Commercial reuse or reproduction may require prior permission; this
private package release does not establish that permission or authorize
public redistribution of the bundled report data. See [the Outlook data
contract](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/docs/outlook.md).

## Contributing and support

Please email <chartwellmacro@gmail.com> for bugs, source changes, or
feature requests. Include a minimal reproducible example, platform and R
version, package version, typed error, and redacted provenance; never
include credentials or private cache files. Pull requests and focused
documentation improvements are welcome—see the repository’s
[contribution
guide](https://github.com/chartwell-macro/readboj/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
for the expected checks and workflow.

# Package index

## Catalogue discovery

- [`build_boj_catalogue_snapshot()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/build_boj_catalogue_snapshot.md)
  : Build a portable, hash-pinned Bank of Japan metadata catalogue
  snapshot
- [`search_boj_catalogue_snapshot()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/search_boj_catalogue_snapshot.md)
  : Search a portable Bank of Japan catalogue snapshot fully offline

## API observations

- [`boj_databases()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_databases.md)
  : List Bank of Japan API databases
- [`boj_metadata()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_metadata.md)
  : Retrieve Bank of Japan series metadata
- [`search_boj_series()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/search_boj_series.md)
  : Search Bank of Japan metadata with bounded output
- [`read_boj_series()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_series.md)
  : Read Bank of Japan observations for exact series codes
- [`read_boj_layer()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_layer.md)
  : Read Bank of Japan observations for a hierarchy layer

## Bulk files and workbooks

- [`list_boj_bulk_files()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/list_boj_bulk_files.md)
  : List the current Bank of Japan bulk-file catalogue
- [`download_boj_bulk()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/download_boj_bulk.md)
  : Download an official Bank of Japan bulk file
- [`read_boj_bulk()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_bulk.md)
  : Read a downloaded official Bank of Japan bulk ZIP or CSV
- [`read_boj_workbook()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_workbook.md)
  : Read a bounded official BOJ XLS/XLSX workbook

## Tankan releases

- [`list_boj_tankan_releases()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/list_boj_tankan_releases.md)
  : List dated official Tankan comprehensive-data releases
- [`list_boj_tankan_assets()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/list_boj_tankan_assets.md)
  : List downloadable assets on a dated Tankan release page
- [`download_boj_tankan_asset()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/download_boj_tankan_asset.md)
  : Download an official dated Tankan asset

## Reproducibility, cache, and provenance

- [`read_boj_snapshot()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_snapshot.md)
  : Parse a local Bank of Japan response snapshot
- [`boj_provenance()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_provenance.md)
  : Extract readboj provenance
- [`boj_cache_prune()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_cache_prune.md)
  : Prune the readboj cache to explicit bounds

## Outlook forecasts and maintenance

- [`list_boj_outlook_releases()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/list_boj_outlook_releases.md)
  : List saved Outlook editions without network access
- [`read_boj_outlook()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_outlook.md)
  : Read saved published Outlook forecast tables
- [`boj_outlook_data_dir()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_outlook_data_dir.md)
  : Location of refreshed Outlook data
- [`boj_outlook_status()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_outlook_status.md)
  : Inspect local Outlook data and updater status
- [`update_boj_outlook()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/update_boj_outlook.md)
  : Incrementally refresh saved Outlook forecast tables
- [`build_boj_outlook_bundle()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/build_boj_outlook_bundle.md)
  : Rebuild a portable Outlook data bundle from the complete raw archive
- [`list_boj_outlook_calendar()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/list_boj_outlook_calendar.md)
  : Discover the official Outlook publication calendar
- [`maintain_boj_outlook()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/maintain_boj_outlook.md)
  : Maintain saved Outlook data and its official next-release schedule
- [`boj_outlook_maintenance_status()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_outlook_maintenance_status.md)
  : Inspect local calendar-aware Outlook maintenance state
- [`list_boj_outlook_releases_raw()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/list_boj_outlook_releases_raw.md)
  : Discover all official Outlook Report editions
- [`read_boj_outlook_raw()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/read_boj_outlook_raw.md)
  : Read published Outlook forecast tables for any official edition

## Service information

- [`boj_api_credit()`](https://chartwell-macro.github.io/readboj/reference/boj_api_credit.md)
  : Prescribed Bank of Japan API credit and terms links
